section_summary: This section continues a British House of Lords debate on Communist violence in Malaya. Speakers dispute whether earlier British policy enabled the insurgency and urge stronger policing, clearer local authority, and caution over constitutional change. They also discuss war damage compensation, trade unions, immigration, food production, and social services.

subfiles.title: Malaya: House of Lords debate
subfiles.about: Peers debate Communist violence in Malaya and British security, constitutional, and economic policy.
subfiles.summary: This continuing debate includes speeches by Viscount Swinton, Lord Milverton, Viscount Marchwood, the Bishop of Truro, Viscount Elibank, Lord Mountevans, the Earl of Scarbrough, and Lord Harlech. They assess the origins of the insurgency and propose stronger police and local executive powers, deportations, and caution over political reform and Singapore's possible inclusion in the Federation. Speakers also dispute war damage funding and discuss trade unions, immigration, health, education, and food supplies. The debate continues beyond page 529.
